items.followUp: Using a velocity-time graph, derive the relation v_f = v_i + at.

accept: final velocity v_f at time t
rubric.why: Identifies the velocities and time interval represented on the graph.
rubric.description: Identify the initial and final velocities on a speed-time graph.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating or clearly showing the initial speed v_i at t = 0 and final speed v_f at time t.

rubric.why: Acceleration is the slope of a speed-time graph.
rubric.description: Relate acceleration to the graph’s slope.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating acceleration equals the change in speed divided by the time taken.

rubric.why: This follows by rearranging the acceleration relation.
rubric.description: Obtain the change in speed in terms of acceleration and time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly rearranging to at = v_f − v_i.

rubric.why: This is the required result.
rubric.description: State the final relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correctly rearranged result.

modelAnswer: On a speed-time graph, let the speed at t = 0 be v_i and the speed at time t be v_f.
Acceleration is the slope of the graph: a = (v_f − v_i)/t.
Therefore, at = v_f − v_i.
Hence, v_f = v_i + at.

items.followUp: A force of 30 N acts on a square surface of side 5 mm. Calculate the pressure on the surface.

rubric.why: Recognizes the applied force from the question.
rubric.description: State the given force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying F = 20 N.

rubric.why: The side must be converted to SI units before calculating area.
rubric.description: Convert the side length to metres.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for converting 10 mm to 0.01 m.

rubric.why: The pin’s lead is square, so its area is side × side.
rubric.description: Calculate the square area in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for calculating A = 1 × 10⁻⁴ m².

rubric.why: Pressure is force per unit area.
rubric.description: Write the pressure formula and substitute the values.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using P = F/A with the given force and calculated area.

rubric.why: This is the pressure obtained from 20 N divided by 1 × 10⁻⁴ m².
rubric.description: Give the pressure with the correct unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 2 × 10⁵ Pa.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 20 N; side = 10 mm = 0.01 m.
Area of the square, A = side² = (0.01 m)² = 1 × 10⁻⁴ m².
Formula: P = F/A.
Substitution: P = 20 N/(1 × 10⁻⁴ m²).
Pressure, P = 2 × 10⁵ Pa.

items.followUp: Define the moment arm of a force and state the SI unit of torque.

rubric.why: Torque describes the turning effect produced by a force.
rubric.description: Define torque.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying torque as the turning or rotational effect of a force.

rubric.why: The turning effect depends on the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the force’s line of action.
rubric.description: Describe the distance used in calculating torque.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying the perpendicular distance from the pivot/axis to the line of action of the force.

rubric.why: This is the relationship defining the magnitude of torque.
rubric.description: Give the torque relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for torque = force × perpendicular distance.

rubric.why: Torque has unit newton metre and produces a rotational direction.
rubric.description: State its unit or describe its rotational sense.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the SI unit N m, or for stating that torque may act clockwise or anticlockwise.

modelAnswer: Torque is the turning effect of a force about a pivot or axis.
Its magnitude depends on the force and the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the force’s line of action; this distance is the moment arm.
Torque = force × perpendicular distance, or τ = Fd.
The SI unit of torque is newton metre (N m); its direction may be clockwise or anticlockwise.

rubric.why: Identifies the given Celsius temperature.
rubric.description: State the given temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the temperature as 80°C.

rubric.why: Uses the Celsius-to-Fahrenheit conversion relation.
rubric.description: Write a valid conversion formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct conversion relation.

rubric.why: Substitutes the known temperature into the conversion relation.
rubric.description: Substitute the value with the correct units or equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution of 80°C.

rubric.why: Evaluates the multiplication correctly before adding 32.
rubric.description: Show the intermediate calculation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining 144 + 32 or an equivalent correct intermediate step.

rubric.why: This is the correct converted temperature.
rubric.description: Give the final temperature in Fahrenheit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 176°F.

modelAnswer: Given: C = 80°C.
Formula: F = (9/5)C + 32.
Substitution: F = (9/5)(80) + 32.
Calculation: F = 144 + 32.
Therefore, F = 176°F.

items.followUp: What is the least count of a measuring instrument? State how the least count of vernier callipers is calculated.

accept: smallest value that can be measured
rubric.why: Least count describes the smallest measurement an instrument can measure accurately.
rubric.description: Define least count.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining it as the smallest measurement or value measurable with the instrument.

rubric.why: This gives the standard vernier callipers least-count relation.
rubric.description: State how the least count of vernier callipers is found.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct relation, such as one main-scale division divided by the number of vernier-scale divisions, or the difference between one MSD and one VSD.

modelAnswer: The least count of vernier callipers is the smallest measurement that can be measured accurately with them.
Least count = value of one main-scale division ÷ number of divisions on the vernier scale (equivalently, 1 MSD − 1 VSD).

items.followUp: Give two examples of difficulties people would face if friction disappeared.

rubric.why: Friction between the feet and the ground is needed for walking without slipping.
rubric.description: State a consequence for walking.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that walking would be impossible or feet would slip due to lack of friction.

rubric.why: Friction provides grip for braking, holding objects and writing.
rubric.description: State another practical consequence.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid consequence, such as vehicles being unable to stop, objects being difficult to hold, or writing being impossible.

modelAnswer: Walking would become impossible because there would be no friction between our feet and the ground to provide grip.
Vehicles could not be stopped by their brakes because friction between the brakes and wheels would be absent.

items.followUp: How does a GPS receiver find the location of a person on Earth?

rubric.why: Identifies the expansion and name of the system.
rubric.description: Name or expand GPS.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying GPS as the Global Positioning System.

rubric.why: GPS uses signals from satellites to determine a receiver’s position.
rubric.description: Describe the system’s purpose or basic operation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that satellite signals are used to determine the receiver’s position on Earth.

modelAnswer: GPS stands for Global Positioning System.
It uses signals from satellites to determine the position of a receiver on Earth.

items.followUp: Draw a distance-time graph for an object moving at constant speed and label both axes.

rubric.why: Time belongs on the horizontal axis, and the graph needs labelled axes.
rubric.description: Label the axes and give a suitable scale.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for time on the horizontal axis and distance on the vertical axis, with a usable scale.

rubric.why: The plotted distances increase by unequal amounts in equal time intervals, producing a non-straight graph and variable speed.
rubric.description: Plot points and show a variable-speed graph.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for plotting a suitable set of points with unequal distance changes per equal time interval and joining them with a non-straight curve.

modelAnswer: Use the horizontal axis for time (s), marked 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 s; use the vertical axis for distance (m), marked 0, 1, 4, 9, 16 m.
Plot the points (0 s, 0 m), (1 s, 1 m), (2 s, 4 m), (3 s, 9 m), and (4 s, 16 m).
Join the points with a smooth upward curve, not a straight line; its changing slope shows variable speed.
